question: A 61-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of a cough productive of clear mucoid sputum. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 33 years. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Chest x-ray shows a 2-cm solid nodule in the periphery of the lower left lobe. A bronchial biopsy of the mass shows numerous mucin-filled epithelial cells lining the alveolar basement membrane. The cells have prominent nucleoli, coarse chromatin, and some cells have multiple nuclei. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Smoking -> Chronic irritation of lung tissue -> Development of lung nodules -> 70% CHAIN: Lung nodule with mucin-filled epithelial cells, prominent nucleoli, coarse chromatin, and multiple nuclei -> Adenocarcinoma -> 80% CHAIN: Clear mucoid sputum -> Mucin production by tumor cells -> Adenocarcinoma -> 75% CHAIN: Chest x-ray showing solid nodule in lower left lobe -> Suspicion for lung cancer -> Adenocarcinoma -> 70%
analysis: The presentation of a 61-year-old man with a history of smoking, cough productive of clear mucoid sputum, and a solid nodule in the lower left lobe is concerning for lung cancer. The histological findings of mucin-filled epithelial cells with prominent nucleoli, coarse chromatin, and multiple nuclei are suggestive of adenocarcinoma, particularly adenocarcinoma in situ.
